messages:
tess: heads-up: found a hang when cancelling an async streaming call in the python SDK sample app. repro with uvloop + aiohttp.
tess: minimal repro:
```
async def reader():
    async for chunk in client.stream(req):
        print(chunk)
# spawn reader, read one chunk, then task.cancel()
```
omar: does server send a 401 or refresh mid-stream? we've seen token refresh races cause weird behavior.
tess: yes, server emits a 401 keepalive and our auth middleware refreshes token. if cancel arrives around same time, socket stays ESTABLISHED and task never finalizes. no exception is shown.
kevin: can you attach netstat and a short traceback? sounds like resp.content.read() is blocked and cancellation doesn't close transport.
tess: gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood-repro/stream-hang-xyz (includes fastapi toy server + test). netstat shows ESTABLISHED.
omar: workaround: add explicit cancel handler that calls resp.close() from another task. also set a short read timeout. not great for onboarding sample.
kevin: SDK idea: attach a done callback to the user task that closes the response object if task cancelled. that may be safer than leaving cleanup to user.
tess: agree. devex will update sample to show a robust cancel pattern and add note about token refresh interactions. filing issue.
qa-bot: created issue #2108 "py-sdk-stream-cancel-hang-auth-refresh" and added labels [devex, repro].
omar: assigning to eng-runtime to verify whether auth refresh grabs locks that block stream cleanup. if so consider making refresh non-blocking for streaming requests.
kevin: small PR suggestion: sample shows how to use asyncio.wait_for around the stream iteration and a cancellation callback that ensures resp.close(). keeps onboarding simple and actionable.
tess: i'll open the PR and include the test that cancels after first chunk so we catch regressions. thanks!
